name: Candlenut, raw
source: Open Food Facts, Kemiri (Nesia) 100 g, label per 100 g
note: Shelled raw kernels as bought; used ground into spice pastes (rempah) a few nuts at a time.

name: Banana blossom, in brine, drained
source: Open Food Facts, Banana Blossom in Brine (Nature's Charm), label per 100 g
note: Canned/jarred blossom (51% blossom, water, salt); label serving 65 g. No measured value for fresh blossom from an allowed source was found. The label kcal is above 4P+4C (22) most likely because it counts fibre it does not list; kept as the label states.

name: Nata de coco, in syrup
source: Open Food Facts, Coconut Gel In Syrup (Chaokoh), label per 100 g
note: Gel cubes with the syrup they're packed in (coconut gel, water, sugar); drained cubes alone would be lower.

name: Thai tea mix, 3-in-1 instant powder
source: Open Food Facts, 3 in 1 Milk Tea Powder (ChaTraMue), label per 100 g
note: Instant powder with sugar and creamer, 20 g sachet per cup. The loose-leaf Thai tea mix is brewed and strained and adds almost nothing itself; its calories come from the condensed/evaporated milk and sugar added.

name: Maggi seasoning, liquid
source: Nestle Professional, MAGGI Liquid Seasoning 1 kg, label per 100 g
note: Hydrolysed wheat protein seasoning; used by the dash (a teaspoon is ~6 g; the label gives 85 kcal per 100 ml). Golden Mountain is a similar soy-based sauce, close enough for the amounts used.

name: Kaffir lime leaves, frozen
source: Open Food Facts, Kaffir Lime Leaves Frozen (Shefs Select), label per 100 g
note: Plain frozen leaves (kcal from the label's 346.8 kJ). A few leaves weigh about 1 g, so this rarely adds anything.

name: Galangal, minced, jarred
source: Open Food Facts, Thai Galangal (minced) (Tiger Tiger), label per 100 g
note: 50% galangal in water and vinegar. No measured value for the fresh rhizome from an allowed source was found; fresh would be roughly double, still trivial in the 5-15 g a dish uses.
